A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PolyPythias study, with all 25 pages, Figures 1–8, Tables 1–5, and Appendices A–E available. Text and rendered-page comparisons support a reliable assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments using 45 additional pre-training runs alongside five existing runs, including downstream evaluations, linguistic probing, and training-map analyses in Sections 3–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original downstream, representational, and training-dynamics results, including the outlier analyses and supplementary plots.

M1.justification: The PolyPythias training procedure, MDL probing objective, HMM training maps, and bag-of-states regression procedures in Sections 2–5 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Pile training data, downstream and bias benchmarks, and seven linguistic probing tasks. Appendix B and the supplementary benchmark coverage are identical.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons across model sizes and seeds are unchanged, including seed-0 predictions for inter-seed agreement and step-0 probes for codelength ratios. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain the same model sizes, 143k-step training budget, checkpoint evaluation schedule, evaluation metrics, and five-state HMM setting in Sections 2–5.

E4.justification: The outlier analyses, cross-size representation correlations, state-transition analyses, and partial-training performance-prediction analysis are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same loss-spike plots.

E5.justification: Both report ten seeds per model size and retain the same statistical reporting: medians and interquartile ranges for downstream metrics, means and standard deviations for probing, and correlation significance reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical and graphical results are unchanged, including Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–8. Both identify 410M seeds 3 and 4 as outliers and report R² = 0.99 for the 410M regression in Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations are identical, including the MDL objective in Equation 1, the codelength ratio, and the Fisher-transformed correlation aggregation in Section 4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusions retain the same contributions and claims concerning the model release, broadly stable training dynamics, consistent learning phases, and identification of outlier runs.

C2.justification: Interpretations and scientific limitations are unchanged, including the 410M model-size ceiling and the need for at least 120k training steps for reliable performance prediction. The added affiliations disclaimer does not qualify the scientific findings.

D1.justification: Implementation and access information remain identical, including GPT-NeoX v1.0 in Appendix A, HMM features in Table 4, and checkpoint and dataset links in Appendix E. The PDFs' external link targets are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the discussion of Pythia, MultiBERTs, and other multi-seed model suites in Section 2.

P1.justification: v2 adds one sentence to Oskar van der Wal's acknowledgments on page 11: "The views expressed in this work do not represent any undisclosed current or future affiliations." The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added acknowledgment sentence causes slight local text reflow and adjusted reference spacing on page 11; the page-1 margin stamp also changes. All figures and tables remain visually identical, and the other 23 pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 adds an affiliations disclaimer and makes associated administrative and local layout changes. The scientific content, evidence, limitations, reproducibility information, and appendices are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
